newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers talks with ministry inconclusive.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers talks with ministry inconclusive.

text.p: Talks between a Greek brokers association (SMEHA) delegation and national economy officials failed to reach a conclusion on a bourse settlement row that has shut the Athens exchange for the past two working days.

The delegation of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA), led by president Panagiotis Kondalexis, headed back to the SMEHA headquarters to resume a general meeting. Asked if the bourse would reopen on Tuesday, Kondalexis said: "We don't know. We are returning to the SMEHA meeting. The process is developing and since it's developing no one can predict anything."
At half past midnight, it was still unclear whether or not broker demands for state guarantees on clearing house operations had been accepted by the ministry.

SMEHA members stopped all activity on the bourse last Friday after one firm, Delta Securities, failed to meet settlement payments. The other SMEHA members said the government must guarantee payment in the future.
Delta has been charged with fraud and its top three officials told not to leave the country.
